syntheses.title: Comparison of Modular Pipeline and Imitation Learning Performance in Autonomous Driving
syntheses.body: Paper A compares the modular pipeline and imitation learning approaches, finding their performance differs by less than 10% (claim 32a49fa0-8395-506b-9794-efc1f7fa2a8f). The modular pipeline shows bimodal performance depending on perception stack success (claim 878110a6-7623-50b9-ab7c-962de08a0fea) and underperforms in navigation tasks in new town and new weather conditions (claim 7d810d97-44b8-5100-a86d-c8d16cb6be0a), with failures linked to perception stack issues under complex weather (claim 56269aff-3ea5-551f-8de8-8c658e1870fe). Paper B focuses on imitation learning improvements, showing that imitation dropout is more effective than re-weighting imitation losses (claims fab08fe9-9a3f-574a-80b1-ef95478330f6 and f1f0ef71-20f9-593d-a66f-3cf2bb27c155). However, pure imitation learning is insufficient even with large datasets and mid-level representations (claims 639f88c8-001d-587a-bae9-390fb3c89dcf and 09081b52-e1ad-5843-9bbc-8565cf5aea59). Mid-level representations facilitate training on simulated or real data and closed-loop testing (claim 5fc32090-a96e-5352-b867-05795d95ae56). Thus, the two papers provide complementary insights into modular pipeline and imitation learning methods, highlighting strengths and limitations in performance and training strategies.
